details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> GDN: use replay instead of rollback (#31669) * GDN: use replay instead of rollback [WIP] * memory : move rs_max with the sequence when find_slot swaps cells find_slot swapped pos/src/rs_pend/seq_id of the cell it moves out of the way, but not rs_max, so that sequence inherited the rollback depth of the cell's previous owner. A smaller value made seq_rm refuse the rollback (#31656), a larger one made snapshot mode restore the previous owner's snapshots. With rs_replay the pending columns are copied along with the state, so rs_max follows the sequence. Without it only the final state is copied and the snapshots stay behind, so the moved sequence gets rs_max 0. * delta_net: drop the graph replay fallback The graph fallback ran the replay as two gdn ops and copied the committed state from the replay gdn when keep, from the main gdn otherwise. Backends whose graph_optimize reorders nodes (Metal, Vulkan) then give keep and non keep ubatches a different node order for the same

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> metal : reserve the top-k scratch only for short rows (#32942) The bitonic top-k path is only faster for short rows. On M5 and M2 Ultra it wins up to 128 columns; above that the radix path is faster. Use the radix path for ncols > 128. The radix path selects in place and needs no scratch, but the buffer type always reserved 2*4 bytes per source element, which is 8 GiB for a 524288 x 2048 score. Reserve the bitonic worst case at the 128-column threshold instead: 2*4*128*nrows, clamped to at least the output tensor size. This keeps the allocation bounded and consistent with the bitonic path.
